subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron runner setup use a bounded portion of the job timeout budget instead of the current fixed 60s ceiling?
rationale: The source-level fix is clear and proof-positive, but the behavior change trades fewer false setup aborts for longer cron-slot occupancy when setup is genuinely stuck.

options.title: Accept bounded setup window
options.body: Land the existing bounded-watchdog PR and treat longer stuck-setup occupancy as the preferred reliability tradeoff.

options.title: Request a tighter cap
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask the PR to reduce the maximum setup window or add more runtime coverage before merge.

options.title: Prefer explicit configurability
options.body: Pause the derived-default PR and require an operator-tunable config surface with upgrade documentation instead.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded setup window
recommendation.body: Land the existing bounded-watchdog PR and treat longer stuck-setup occupancy as the preferred reliability tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: The open PR author owns the current focused implementation path and proof for the decision under review.
